lines.speaker: v
lines.text: [urgently] You're crossing a beach at low tide... and your legs sink into the sand.

lines.speaker: v
lines.text: [ominously] It's quicksand. And it won't let go.

lines.speaker: v
lines.text: [building] Your instinct says yank your leg out. Don't. Pulling one foot out fast takes about as much force as lifting a car.

lines.speaker: v
lines.text: [urgently] And don't let a friend haul you out either. The sand holds on so hard, they could badly hurt you.

lines.speaker: v
lines.text: [curious] Here's what the movies get wrong: you can't sink all the way under. Quicksand is about twice as dense as your body, so you float, roughly waist deep.

lines.speaker: v
lines.text: [dryly] So the sand isn't what kills you. [short pause] [ominously] On a beach... the tide is.

lines.speaker: v
lines.text: [confident] The move: stop struggling. Wiggle your legs slowly, in small circles. That lets water seep in and loosens the sand around you.

lines.speaker: v
lines.text: [confident] Then lean back, spread your arms, and let your body float on top. Inch by inch, work your way to firm ground.

lines.speaker: v
lines.text: [curious] So... would you have kept pulling, or leaned back?
